_comment: skfem helmholtz#2: omitting the +i*k*u FacetBasis term reflects. Verified 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1 on a one-element-thick MeshQuad strip (k=8, 20 elements/wavelength, 4 wavelengths, 162 DOFs, u=1 driven at x=0) -- the claim's 2D MeshTri picture scaled to the cheapest geometry that still carries an outgoing wave. Without the ABC the standing-wave ratio max|u|/min|u| is ~1.6e2 and the |u| maxima are spaced at exactly lambda/2; with @BilinearForm(dtype=complex) 1j*k*u*v on FacetBasis('right') the SWR falls to ~1.004 with |u| ~ 1 everywhere and the phase matching exp(-ikx). Also pins that the SHIPPED helmholtz_2d template's default-dtype ABC block (nnz 0) gives a bit-identical solution to having no ABC at all. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 flips the wrong variant's selector ABC from 'none' to 'complex', i.e. adds the documented @BilinearForm(dtype=complex) 1j*k*u*v term on FacetBasis('right') at the pathology site; the measured SWR falls from 1.6e2 to 1.004. Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1: the unmutated run matches all 11 expect_in_output strings; T2_MUTATE=1 removes 'no_abc_swr_gt_10=True', 'default_dtype_abc_identical_to_no_abc=True' and 'abc_improves_swr_by_gt_50x=True' so the fixture goes red. NOTE 'n_peaks_ge_6=True' and 'peak_spacing_matches_half_wavelength=True' SURVIVE the mutation: local_maxima() is amplitude-blind, so the 0.4% residual ripple of the fully absorbed wave still shows 8 maxima spaced at lambda/2 -- those two carry weight only together with the SWR gate. Re-run: T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py CAVEAT found while adding the mutation control (assertion NOT changed): 'n_peaks_ge_6' and 'peak_spacing_matches_half_wavelength' survive a PERFECT ABC. Measured with the ABC installed: no_abc_n_peaks=8 and peak_spacing=0.39270 against half_wavelength=0.39270, while with_abc_amplitude_dev=0.0041. local_maxima() is amplitude-blind, so a 0.4 percent residual ripple on a purely outgoing wave satisfies the 'standing-wave interference at half a wavelength' claim exactly as a 160:1 standing wave does. Only the SWR gate discriminates.
